::: {.why}
Every result in this phase is one you produced and evaluated; a live external tournament with a held-out future removes that degree of freedom entirely, and it is the one public track record this industry recognises.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Submit a model to Numerai and understand what its scoring metric measures.
- Say what the obfuscated features and era structure prevent, and what they do not.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Fit one of your existing model configurations on the Numerai training data and submit. The features are obfuscated, so you cannot bring any prior about what they mean, which removes the leakage channel that comes from knowing which period a feature was constructed in.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Read the documentation on the scoring metric and note that it is a correlation with era-wise neutralisation, which is the same construct as your information coefficient with cross-sectional neutralisation. Then note what obfuscation does not prevent, which is overfitting to the training eras, and check whether the era structure lets you build the purged splitter you already have.
:::
:::

## The running strategy

::: {.project}
A model is submitted to Numerai, which gives the year an external, live-scored track record on data where no look-ahead is available to you, alongside the internal results you produced and evaluated yourself.
:::
